message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need to know | |---------|-----------------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are tallied from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck works best with 4–8). | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Draw Two,” two “Skip,” two “Reverse”). 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four.” | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card to start the discard pile; if it’s a special card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Play** | 1. **Match** a card from your hand to the top of the discard pile by **color, number, or symbol**.
2. If you can’t match, **draw one card** from the draw pile.
3. If the drawn card can be played, you may do so immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | • **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction (acts like Skip in a 2‑player game).
• **Wild** – You choose the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the next color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk a challenge.) | | **Going “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. Failure to do so means you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards still held by opponents: numbers = face value, Draw Two/Skip/Reverse = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Winning the Game** | First player to reach the target score (commonly 500) wins. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of the current color** – it’s easy to forget after a Wild. 2. **Use Draw Twos and Skips strategically** – they’re great for blocking opponents who are close to winning. 3. **Watch for “Wild Draw Four”** – only play it when you truly have no other options; otherwise you risk a challenge. 4. **Plan ahead** – try to keep a mix of colors so you can always play something. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
